title: WISH e IF ONLY
subtitle: Wish and if only · deseos y lamentos

explain.es: Wish e if only equivalen a ojalá o me gustaría que… cuando el deseo es irreal: algo que no es así ahora, algo que no pasó o algo que nos molesta. El gran truco: el verbo da un paso atrás en el tiempo. Igual que en español usamos el subjuntivo (ojalá tuviera, ojalá hubiera tenido), en inglés usamos el pasado.
explain.en: Wish and if only express unreal wishes, regrets and complaints. The verb moves one step back in time.

explain.title: 1 · Deseos sobre el presente
explain.es: Para algo que no es verdad ahora y nos gustaría que lo fuera. Usamos wish + past simple, aunque hablamos del presente. La realidad es siempre la contraria: I wish I lived closer = I don't live closer. En español: ojalá + imperfecto de subjuntivo (ojalá viviera).
explain.en: For something that isn't true now. We use wish + past simple, although we are talking about the present.

examples.es: Ojalá viviera más cerca del trabajo.
Le gustaría tener más tiempo libre.

examples.en: I wish I didn't have to work this weekend.
examples.es: Ojalá no tuviera que trabajar este fin de semana.

explain.title: Truco del paso atrás
explain.es: Wish siempre mira hacia atrás: el verbo retrocede un tiempo. presente → pasado (have → had), can → could, pasado → past perfect (went → had gone), will → would. Truco del español: si dices ojalá + tuviera → past simple; si dices ojalá + hubiera tenido → past perfect.
explain.en: Wish always moves one step back: present → past, can → could, past → past perfect, will → would.

explain.title: 2 · WISH + COULD
explain.es: Para habilidades o posibilidades que no tenemos: wish + could + infinitivo. could es el pasado de can: el mismo paso atrás de siempre. En español: ojalá supiera / ojalá pudiera.
explain.en: For abilities or possibilities we don't have: wish + could + infinitive.

examples.en: We wish we could come to your wedding, but we'll be abroad.
examples.es: Ojalá pudiéramos ir a tu boda, pero estaremos en el extranjero.

examples.en: He wishes he could afford a new car.
examples.es: Le encantaría poder permitirse un coche nuevo.

explain.title: 3 · ¿WAS o WERE?
explain.es: Con el verbo be, después de wish podemos usar were con todas las personas (I, he, she, it). Es la forma más cuidada y la que se espera en un examen. was también se oye mucho en conversación informal. ¡Pero nunca am / is!
explain.en: After wish we can use were with all persons. Was is common in informal speech. Never am / is.

examples.en: I wish I were on a beach right now.
examples.es: Ojalá estuviera en una playa ahora mismo.

explain.title: El paso atrás
head: Realidad · Reality
Deseo · Wish
rows: I wish I didn't have to work.
I'm not going to the concert.
I wish I were going to the concert.
I wish I hadn't spent all my money.
I didn't go to the party.
I wish I had gone to the party.
explain.note: Afirmativa ↔ negativa: la realidad y el deseo van al revés.
explain.note_en: Positive ↔ negative: reality and wish are opposites.

explain.title: 4 · Lamentos sobre el pasado
explain.es: Para arrepentirnos de algo que pasó (o que no pasó). Ya no se puede cambiar. Usamos wish + past perfect (had + participio). En español: ojalá hubiera… o me arrepiento de…
explain.en: To express regret about the past: wish + past perfect (had + past participle).

examples.en: I wish I had studied harder for the exam.
examples.es: Ojalá hubiera estudiado más para el examen.

examples.en: She wishes she hadn't sold her old flat.
examples.es: Se arrepiente de haber vendido su antiguo piso.
Ojalá no hubiera mandado ese mensaje.

explain.title: 5 · Quejas: WISH + WOULD
explain.es: Para quejarnos de algo que hace otra persona (o algo externo, como el tiempo) y que queremos que cambie. Expresa enfado o impaciencia. Ojo: el sujeto tiene que ser distinto: no se dice I wish I would. Tampoco se usa con verbos de estado: I wish you would be taller.
explain.en: To complain about what someone else does and say we want it to change. Not with the same subject: <s>I wish I would</s>.

examples.es: A ver si dejas de interrumpirme.

examples.en: I wish my neighbours wouldn't play their music so loud.
examples.es: Ojalá mis vecinos no pusieran la música tan alta.

explain.title: 6 · IF ONLY
explain.es: If only funciona igual que wish (mismos tiempos: past simple, past perfect, would) pero es más emotivo e intenso: ¡Ojalá…! / ¡Si al menos…! Suele ir al principio de la frase y con signo de exclamación.
explain.en: If only works like wish (same tenses) but it is stronger and more emotional.
formula: *If only* + sujeto + past simple / past perfect / would

explain.note: Wish siempre mira un paso atrás: presente → pasado · pasado → past perfect · can → could · will → would.
explain.note_en: Wish always moves one step back.

explain.title: WISH o HOPE
explain.es: hope = deseo posible, real (presente o futuro normal). wish = deseo irreal (paso atrás). En español los dos pueden ser ojalá: pregúntate si de verdad puede pasar.

explain.title: Otros usos de WISH
head: Estructura
Significado
Ejemplo
rows: We wish you a merry Christmas.
I wish to make a complaint.
Blow out the candles and make a wish!
explain.note: Aquí no hay paso atrás: I wish you a happy birthday = Te deseo un feliz cumpleaños.
explain.note_en: No step back in these expressions.

items.bad: I wish I have a bigger flat.
items.good: I wish I had a bigger flat.
items.why: Deseo sobre el presente → paso atrás: past simple.

items.bad: I wish I didn't go to that party last night.
items.good: I wish I hadn't gone to that party last night.
items.why: Lamento sobre el pasado → past perfect.

items.bad: I wish I would be taller.
items.why: wish + would no va con el mismo sujeto ni con estados.
items.why_en: No would with the same subject or state verbs.

items.bad: I wish you pass your driving test.
items.good: I hope you pass your driving test.

items.bad: I wish I can play the guitar.
items.good: I wish I could play the guitar.
items.why: can da un paso atrás → could.

items.bad: If only I would know the answer!
items.why: if only funciona como wish: past simple.

items.bad: I wish I had went to university.
items.good: I wish I had gone to university.

items.bad: I hope I were on holiday.

items.es: ¿Es sobre el presente? → wish + past simple (o could / were).
items.en: Present → wish + past simple / could / were.
Complaint → would. More emotion → If only.

lines.en: How did the B2 exam go?
Terrible. I wish I had started studying earlier.
lines.es: Fatal. Ojalá hubiera empezado a estudiar antes.

lines.en: The listening. If only I understood British accents better!
lines.es: El listening. ¡Si al menos entendiera mejor el acento británico!

lines.en: I'm sure you did better than you think. I hope you pass!
lines.es: Seguro que te ha ido mejor de lo que crees. ¡Ojalá apruebes!

lines.en: Thanks. And I wish my brother would stop asking me about it!
lines.es: Gracias. ¡Y a ver si mi hermano deja de preguntarme por él!

lines.en: Ha! Come on, let's go for a coffee. I wish I could help more.
lines.es: ¡Ja! Venga, vamos a tomar un café. Ojalá pudiera ayudarte más.

lines.en: Coffee helps. If only I'd known the exam was this hard!
lines.es: El café ayuda. ¡Ojalá hubiera sabido que el examen era tan difícil!

exercises.text_title: Ask Rosie: your problems, my advice
text: Dear Rosie, I'm 19 and in my first year at university. I wish I had chosen a different degree. I'm studying Law because my parents wanted me to, but I've always loved design. If only I had been brave enough to tell them! — Lucía

Dear Lucía, you're not the only one! Lots of students wish they could go back and choose again. But it isn't too late. I hope you talk to your parents soon. They might understand more than you think. — Rosie

Dear Rosie, my flatmate drives me crazy. I wish he would wash his dishes, and I wish he wouldn't play video games until 3 a.m. I also wish our flat were bigger, because I have nowhere to escape! — Tom, Leeds

items.q: Lucía is studying the degree she always wanted.
items.why: She wishes she had chosen design.

items.q: Lucía told her parents she wanted to study design.
items.why: If only I had been brave enough to tell them!

items.q: Rosie thinks it is too late to change.
items.why: She says it isn't too late.

items.q: What does Lucía regret?
items.a: Choosing Law instead of design (and not telling her parents).

items.q: Why does Rosie write 'I hope you talk' and not 'I wish you talked'?
items.a: Because it's a real possibility (hope = possible).

items.q: What two things does Tom want his flatmate to change?
items.a: He wants him to wash his dishes and to stop playing video games until 3 a.m.

items.q: Which of Tom's wishes is not a complaint about his flatmate?
items.a: I wish our flat were bigger.

items.q: What is the reality behind 'I wish our flat were bigger'?
items.a: Their flat is small (it isn't big enough).
